title: Contributor orientation, layering ratchets and a recurring read-only structural review
problem: Six entry files gave five reading orders; 13 of 45 top-level directories had no README and 16 were missing from the README layout; docs/ had no index and docs/collaboration's ~170 records had no current-vs-historical signal; nothing guarded package layering (9 two-way package dependencies, one import out of the published boundary package); and SOP-06's measures were defined but never measured, with no recurring review. Contributors' records show orientation and coordination friction recurring (docs/collaboration/CONTRIBUTOR-PAIN-POINTS-2026-11-05.md).
baseline: #196 head 3a2ba265: scripts/repo_review.py reports 38 hard findings; the six new map tests fail; no scheduled workflow exists.

alternatives.name: Rewrite and consolidate the entry files into one
alternatives.description: Merge AGENTS, CLAUDE, CONTRIBUTING, README agent sections and copilot instructions into one file and delete the rest
disadvantages: deletes institutional memory against the founder's 'delete nothing'
CLAUDE.md and copilot instructions are client entry points that must exist
rewrites founder-correction text other tests and receipts reference
alternatives.revival_evidence: A founder ruling that the entry files may be rewritten, and receipts no longer pin AGENTS.md text

alternatives.name: Adopt import-linter as a dependency
alternatives.description: Configure the import-linter package with layered contracts
disadvantages: a new dependency for two rules
its contracts would duplicate the KEPT tables the weekly report also needs
alternatives.revival_evidence: More than three layering rules are wanted, or the ratchet's AST scan misses a real import

alternatives.name: Comment-based monthly reminders on board #96
alternatives.description: Post a recurring review prompt as an issue comment
disadvantages: an outward posting effect every week
alternatives.revival_evidence: The founder asks for review prompts on the board

do_nothing_option.expected_outcome: Agents keep entering through whichever order they see first; new undocumented directories and package cycles keep accumulating unnoticed; SOP-06 stays NOT_MEASURED
disadvantages: recurring stale-context and misrouted starts documented in the register
no trigger ever runs SOP-06 or protocol section 6

roles.position: The founder asked for exactly this: delete nothing, agent comprehension, contributor engagement, regular review. The package adds and removes no obligation. Adopt as draft; the order places the latest founder corrections first and states that a founder record wins any disagreement
material_concerns: the canonical reading order must not silently reorder founder corrections

roles.position: One instrument (scripts/repo_review.py) serves the unit tests and the weekly report, so the rule exists once. Only cycles and boundary escapes are ratcheted, not ordinary imports. Keep the ratchet narrow
material_concerns: a ratchet on every edge would force KEPT-table edits in parallel PRs and recreate generated-record conflicts (pain point P-1/P-3)

roles.position: Self-review by one session, not independent. The weekly workflow is inert until a founder merge to main. Map tests can be satisfied with an empty README. Label the proxies as proxies in the report; leave README quality to the monthly review instead of a length rule
material_concerns: a README containing only a heading passes the rule
word-count proxies could be mistaken for SOP-06 measures

roles.position: The tests run in seconds inside the existing suite; the workflow is 10 minutes, weekly, read-only; no job timeout or pin changes. Acceptable; the added cost is under 10 seconds per suite run
material_concerns: Canonical job 1 is already near its 120-minute limit (P-2)

roles.position: No posting, no labels, no tokens with write scope; friction reports are voluntary; nothing ranks contributors. The form asks for the obstacle, not the person responsible; keep it that way
material_concerns: a friction form could become a blame channel

evidence.claim: The map guards fail before and pass after
evidence.reference: local run on 3a2ba265 with the new tests copied in: 6 failed, 14 passed; after: 21 passed
python scripts/repo_review.py --check: 38 findings before, exit 0 after

21 affected test files, 599 passed and 2 skipped, plus test_data_exposure_ledger 14/14; governance.integrity --check exit 0; check_authority_singleton, check_schema_refs and check_release_exclusions exit 0
evidence.finding: confirmed after installing requirements-dev and requirements-cognition

counterevidence.claim: Guards that are not in CI still protect
counterevidence.reference: scripts/ci/check_seed_mutants.py: 7/7 caught with the dependencies installed, but first 5/7 here because rfc3161_client was missing
counterevidence.finding: a gate outside CI can be silently environment-broken; recorded as S-3

counterevidence.claim: A docs index ends orientation drift
counterevidence.finding: it cannot tell a stale dated record from a current one; only #96 and the integration head can

pass_1.intended_outcome: Two-hop orientation from AGENTS.md for any contributor; drift caught per PR; a measured, recurring review

advantages.statement: One rule source for tests and report
advantages.amplified_value: the weekly report and a PR cannot disagree about a rule
each tolerated cycle is visible with its reason and can only be removed

advantages.statement: A real latent defect surfaced (provenance/witness.py lazy import outside the boundary package)
advantages.amplified_value: recorded where the next boundary release will see it

disadvantages.statement: The weekly schedule cannot run until the workflow is on main
disadvantages.redesigned_response: REVIEW_CADENCE.md states this and gives the manual command for intake until then

disadvantages.statement: Edits to AGENTS.md change the text receipts read at head
disadvantages.redesigned_response: The block is additive and at the top; receipts reread AGENTS.md at head anyway
The uppercase file is marked with the canonical one; the merge is a founder decision because foundry commissioning copies the lowercase template's bytes

comparisons.simplest_viable_alternative: READMEs and an index without tests (drifts again)
comparisons.reversible_experiment: this package: revert one commit; nothing to migrate

rejected_alternatives.name: Ratchet every cross-package edge
rejected_alternatives.rejection_reason: Forces table edits in ordinary feature PRs, recreating merge conflicts
rejected_alternatives.revival_evidence: Layering decay measured despite the narrow ratchet

pass_2.attack_summary: Attacked the strengthened package for new bureaucracy, gaming and fragility.

new_weaknesses.statement: An empty README satisfies the map test
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: The monthly review samples new READMEs; a length rule was rejected as noise

new_weaknesses.statement: Five rhythms could add more process than they save
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: REVIEW_CADENCE.md kill criteria: two empty months reduce it to weekly plus quarterly; a rhythm nobody acted on for a quarter is killed

new_weaknesses.statement: The import scan reads every package file and could slow down as greg grows
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: It is an AST walk taking about 6 s on 169k lines; it is measured in each weekly report

pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.rationale: GitHub restriction; the manual path exists
pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.review_trigger: merge of the integration line to main
a receipt check failure that cites AGENTS.md

pass_2.final_design: As implemented: additive docs, two narrow ratchets, one read-only weekly workflow, a friction form, a dated pain-point register and the cadence with kill criteria. Proposed for adoption as a reversible experiment with the kill criteria below.

residual_risks.risk: The weekly report is produced but nobody reads it
residual_risks.mitigation: Assigned to the integration owner's intake; the kill criterion applies
Labelled as such; independent review requested on #96
residual_risks.review_trigger: a different session reviews the PR

entries.position: Without independent review and without the schedule live, the package proves only that the rules hold today, not that the cadence improves anything.
entries.rationale: SOP-06 asks for a measured improvement, not a document
entries.evidence_threshold: After the first five coordinated PRs, if SOP-06's measures show no change, regress the monthly and quarterly rhythms
entries.review_trigger: the fifth completed coordinated PR after adoption

authority_impact.approver: Alfonso Lopez (merge to main activates the schedule); #196 integration owner (intake)

migration_plan: None. Additive files and edits; no data, schema, pin or digest changes.

steps: Revert the package's commits, or decline intake into #196
Delete nothing else: the register and intent record stay as history if the founder regresses the cadence

kill_criteria: The review workflow ever gains a write permission or a posting step
A KEPT table grows instead of shrinking
Two consecutive monthly reviews with no actionable finding and no friction report (simplify)
A rhythm nobody acted on for a quarter (kill that rhythm)
decision_owner: Offered as a reversible EXPERIMENT (pass 2). Alfonso Lopez decides adoption, the PR template merge (P-10) and F-1; the #196 integration owner decides intake; session_01KucyfnCuSTnjx5Fa6T4A3d owns the reversible draft. This is self-review by one session through five lenses, not five independent reviewers.
review_trigger: Canonical CI on the PR head; an independent review by a different session; the first weekly report on main; the first five coordinated PRs (SOP-06)
